name: Smt. P. T. Usha
education: Pre-degree Educated at Providence Women’s College, Calicut, Kerala
present_address: Flat No.601, Swarn Jayanti Sadan Deluxe, Dr. Bishambar Das Marg, New Delhi- 110001
permanent_address: P. T. Usha Road, Payyoli P.O., District - Kozhikode, Kerala - 673522
books: Golden Girl : The Autobiography of P.T. Usha, 1986; a number of books have been written on her life and achievements, including, (i) Ore Oru Usha, 1986, (ii) P.T. Usha: the Pride of India, 1987, (iii) Udan Pari,1987 (Hindi version of P.T. Usha: the Pride of India), (iv) P.T. Usha - A Case Study, 2002 and (v) P.T. Usha -The Sprint Queen, 2022
hobbies: President, Indian Olympic Association; became the first woman to be elected President of the I.O.A.; started the Usha School of Athletics at Kinaloor, Kozhikode, after retirement from sports
countries_visited: U.K., Russia, U.S.A., South Korea, Muscat, Morocco, Belgium, China, Poland, Samoa Island, Vietnam, Brazil, Thailand, Indonesia, Japan and Kazakhstan
other_information: Conferred, (i) Arjuna Award, 1984, (ii) Padma Shri 1984, (iii) Best Athlete of Asia, 1984, 1985, 1986, 1987 and 1989, (iv) Marshal Tito award for the best Railway Sportsperson in 1984, 1985, 1986, 1989 and 1990, World Railway Best Athlete, 1985, (v) Indian and Kerala Sports Journalists Award for the year 1984, 1985, 1986, 1987, 1989 and 1999, (vi) Chinese Journalist Award in 1985,1986 1989, (vii) World Trophy for Best Athlete, 1985 and 1986, (viii) Greatest woman athlete, in 1985 Jakarta Asian Athletic Meet, (ix) the Adidas Golden Shoe for Best Athlete of Asia, Seoul Asian Games, 1986, (x) Saraswathi Ratan Puraskar by State Government of Andhra Pradesh, 1986, (xi) Mahila Shiromani Award in 1992, (xii) Best Sportsperson of the century, 2000 by the Indian Olympic Association, (xiii) Sthree Ratnam Award, 2012, (xiv) ‘Veteran Pin Award’, 2018 by IAAF and (xv) outstanding contribution to Indian Sports Award by BBC 2020; conferred, Honorary D.Litt. by (i) Kannur University, Kannur, Kerala, 2000, (ii) Calicut University, Kerala, 2018, (iii) Vels Institute of Science, Technology and Advanced Studies (VISTAS), Chennai, Tamil Nadu, 2019, (iv) I.T.M. University, Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, 2019, (v) Vinayaka Medical Mission’s Research Foundation University, Salem, Tamil Nadu, 2022 and (vi) Central University of Kerala, 2023; Honorary D.Sc. by IIT Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, 2017; participated in many major sports events including the Olympics Games, Moscow, 1980, Asian Games, New Delhi, 1982, Asian Track and Field games, Kuwait, 1983, International meet, at Inglewood U.S.A, 1984, Olympics Games, Los Angeles, 1984, Olympics Games, Seoul, 1988, Olympics Games, Atlanta, 1996, Asian Track and Field Meet, Jakarta, etc.; secured more than 800 medals in the various National level athletic competitions; made World Records, in the 1985 Asian Track and Field Meet at Jakarta (Indonesia); secured 5 gold medals in 100 meters, 200, 400, 400 m. hurdles and 4x400 m. relay; as a national athletic coach, produced 2 Olympians and 8 International athletes with athletes under her training having secured 79 International medals for the country and more than 700 National medals (they still hold 4 National Records in events like 400 m and 800 m at the senior and Junior levels)
